# 3b Routing lists, ownership, server-hostname guard: contract

**Read first:** [build README → Phase 3](./README.md#phase-3-routing), [routing lists](../processes/routing/routing-lists.md), [service management](../processes/routing/service-management.md) (its guard edge case), [routing module → Routing lists](../modules/routing.md#routing-lists), [ADR 0013](../adr/0013-one-owner-service-per-domain.md), [architecture](../architecture.md) (the rule that Proxier's traffic to its servers must never enter the router's VPN), `internal/modules/servers/ports.go` and the new-server form (`servers/provision`, `servers/pages/newserver.go`), designs `RP-Lists`, `RP-List`, `RP-Service`, `RP-Custom-service`, and the **As built** of 3a and 2a (sortable lists, `data-cursor`, stale orders answered 200 with a notice under htmx).

**Done when:** routing lists can be created, renamed and described, made the default, and deleted (refused for the default, and while targets follow a list unless they are moved to another one in the same step); a list's services can be added (ticked from existing services, or a new selector through Add service), removed and reordered by drag, `J`/`K` and ↑/↓; ownership is computed by the pure `own` package and shown (owned / total per service on the list page; "owned by …", "covered by …" and "left out" notes on the service page; "covered by" hints in the custom editor); the server-hostname guard refuses every save that would put a name covering a server's hostname into a list, naming the server, leaves such names out when an upstream snapshot brings them, and makes servers' provisioning refuse a hostname a list covers; every list change marks its targets; every checklist line has its test.

Not in 3b: targets (3d, 3e: the Targets areas say "No routers or Shadowrocket configs follow Main yet"), rejected-snapshot warnings (3c), **Refresh all** (3c).

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Ownership | `own.Compute(members, servers, exclude)` over the list's services **in order**, each with its accepted snapshot. First, names that trip the guard (`guarded`) or are in `exclude` (a router's infra pins, 3e: `pinned`) are taken out of every set: they are installed by nobody and cover nothing. Then, for service *i*: a **suffix** name *d* is dropped as `covered` when another service *j ≠ i* has a proper parent of *d* as a suffix, else as `owned` when an earlier service has *d* as a suffix; an **exact** name *d* is dropped as `covered` when another service has *d* or a parent of *d* as a suffix, else as `owned` when an earlier service has *d* as an exact name. Everything else is the service's: installed under its tag. Names under the service's **own** suffixes stay (mtvpn compatibility, Build README defaults). | ADR 0013; routing-lists.md#rules. |
| Why a name is dropped | `own.Drop{Name, Exact, Reason, By, Via}`: `covered` (By = the covering service's tag, Via = the covering suffix), `owned` (By = the owner's tag), `guarded` (By = the server's name, Via = its hostname), `pinned` (Via = the router's comment). Pages say "covered by anthropic.com (anthropic)", "owned by anthropic (first in Main)", "left out: covers nl-1.hosts.tikhonnnnn.com (nl-1)". | ADR 0013 consequence: "the service page has to show 'owned elsewhere'". |
| The guard | `own.Covering(name, exact, servers)`: a suffix name covers a hostname that equals it or ends with `.` + it; an exact name only one that equals it. The hostnames are `ServerHostnames.Servers(ctx)`: every non-retired server's management and proxy hostnames (a retiring one included). A nil port means there is nothing to guard. | routing-lists.md#rules. |
| Guard on saves | Refused, nothing written, naming the first covering name: adding a service to a list (`lists.Add`, also from Add service with lists ticked), saving a custom service that is in a list (`services.SaveCustom` through `Deps.Check = lists.CheckService`). The answer is `*lists.GuardError{List, Service, Domain, Server, Hostname}`: "Adding tikhonnnnn.com would cover nl-1.hosts.tikhonnnnn.com, the hostname of nl-1. It wasn't saved." Right after the refused transaction rolls back, one `routing.list_refused_server_hostname{domain, server, hostname, service}` per list it would have broken is recorded in its own `Write` (subject that list). | "Saving is refused, naming the server and the domain." |
| Guard on refresh | A snapshot accepted later (3c) or a switched source may bring a covering name: it is accepted, `own.Compute` leaves the name out (`guarded`), and the list page shows the warning "v2fly:foo has tikhonnnnn.com, which covers nl-1.hosts.tikhonnnnn.com (nl-1): left out of what targets get." No event (it's a computed state, shown while it lasts). | Build README defaults: a refresh is never refused for one name. |
| Guard for provisioning | servers declares `RoutingGuard` and `SetRouting`; routing's `Module.Guard()` implements it over **every** listed name of every list (dropped ones included: any listed name counts). `servers/provision` asks it with the new server's management and proxy hostnames before creating anything; a hit is a form error under the summary (422): "nl-3.hosts.tikhonnnnn.com is covered by tikhonnnnn.com (my-sites) in Main: Proxier's checks would go into the tunnel. Take it out of the list first." Nil guard: nothing checked. | routing-lists.md edge case "provisioning refused on the form". |
| ServerHostnames | servers' port becomes `Servers(ctx) ([]ServerHostname, error)`: `{ServerID, Name, Hostnames []string, IP}` for every server whose state isn't `retired`, by id, hostnames without empty or duplicate ones. The old `Hostnames` method goes (it had no caller). | The guard names the server. |
| Lists | Name trimmed 1–60, unique by exact match (`lists.err.name_taken`); description ≤ 1 000. `routing.list_created{name}`; an edit records `routing.list_updated{changes}` with the changed fields' names, nothing when unchanged. **Make default** moves the mark in one statement pair and records `list_updated{changes: "default"}` on the new default; on the current default it changes nothing. | routing-lists.md steps 2–4. |
| Members | `routing_list_services` rows: list, service, dense `position` 1…n, `added_at`. **Add** appends the ticked services **in tag order** after the last one, skipping any already in it; **Remove** re-densifies; each records `routing.list_updated{added \| removed: tags comma-joined}` and marks `Change{Lists: [id], Why}`. A service can be in any number of lists. | 2a's pattern for subscription servers. |
| Reorder | As 2a: **drag** posts the whole `order=<id>,…` to `/routing/lists/:id/services/order` (a permutation of the current members, else `lists.ErrStaleOrder`: 200 with the area as stored and a gold line under htmx, 409 without); **`J`/`K`** and the row's ↓/↑ post `/services/:service/move` with `dir=down\|up`. A change records `list_updated{reordered: true}` and marks the list; no change records nothing. Answers re-render the Services area with `data-cursor` on the moved row. | Sortable lists (2a). |
| Undo | After a reorder (drag, `J`/`K` or ↑/↓) the Services area answers with a band (the user chose this design extra): "Moved youtube above google" (or "below …"), "14 domains change owner (googlevideo.com, ytimg.com…)" from `own.Moved(before, after)` (or "No domain changes owner."), the targets that get it ("Home and iPhone re-sync.", from 3d/3e on), and **Undo** (key `u`, `data-key="u"`). Undo posts the previous order to the order route with `expect=<the order right after the move>`: when the current order isn't that any more, it is stale (as above); otherwise it is an ordinary reorder (`list_updated{reordered: true}`, marked) and its own band offers Undo again. The band lives in the swapped area, so it is gone after a reload; without htmx the post redirects and shows no band. | `RP-List`. |
| Delete | `lists.Delete(ctx, id, moveTo, actor)`: the default → `lists.ErrDefault` ("Make another list the default first"); targets following it (rows of `routing_routers` and `routing_shadowrocket`, read and moved through `store`: both tables exist from 3a, and `lists` can't call the 3d/3e services, which depend on it) and `moveTo = 0` → `*lists.HasTargetsError{Targets}`; with `moveTo` (another list): in one `Write`, each router moves (`routing.router_updated{changes: list, from, to}`), each config moves (`routing.shadowrocket_updated{changes: list}`), the moved routers are marked `Change{Routers}`, then the list goes (`routing.list_deleted{name, moved}`). Its memberships go with it (`ON DELETE CASCADE`); its services stay. | routing-lists.md step 5. |
| The view | `lists.View(ctx, id, exclude)` loads the members in order with their accepted snapshots (decoded from text), asks the hostnames port once, and runs `own.Compute`. Every page, Shadowrocket fetch (3d) and sync (3e) uses it. Nothing is cached. | Build README "Ownership is computed, never stored". |
| Counts | A member's **owned / total**: names it installs / names in its snapshot. The list's domain count: the sum of owned names. | `RP-List`, `RP-Lists`. |
| Warnings | `lists.Warnings(ctx, id)`: guard refusals recorded for this list in the last 7 days (from `events.List`, newest first, at most 5); guarded names left out now (from the view). 3c adds rejected snapshots waiting and refreshes failing among its services. | `RP-List` warnings area. |
| Add services | `GET /routing/lists/:id/add`: a page styled as a dialog: a filter field (`?q=`, htmx), the services not in the list as checkboxes (tag, selector, source, count), **Add N services** (primary). Under it: "Or add a new one" with the selector field, posting to Add service with `lists=<id>` ticked, and (3c) "Search the catalog". | ui/README "Add services (picker with search)". |
| Add service with lists | 3a's add page gains **Add to routing lists**: a checkbox per list, the default list ticked. With lists ticked the page calls `lists.AddNew(ctx, sel, listIDs, actor)`: `services.Prepare` (parse, tag, resolve: no write), then `lists.CheckSet` (the guard over the resolved set for those lists, refused as above), then one `Write`: `services.CreateTx` and `AddTx` for each list (one `list_updated{added}` each, marked). `services` never imports `lists` (lists imports services); orchestration that needs both lives in `lists` or in the caller. | service-management.md step 5. |
| Add to lists (a service) | `GET/POST /routing/services/:id/lists`: the lists it isn't in, as checkboxes. The search page (3c), discovery (3g) and the service page's Actions use it. | catalog-search.md "Add to lists…". |
| Custom editor hints | Each row shows "covered by openai in Main" when another service of a list the service is in has the name, or a suffix above it (`own.CoveredBy`); the footer says "Saving changes what the targets of Main get." (3e names the routers). A guard refusal shows above the table and keeps the edits. | service-management.md step 4. |
| Service page | The line names its lists ("in Main and Parents"); **Source** lists them with positions ("Main #4 · Parents #2"); **Domains** notes per list the names it doesn't install there (owned, covered, left out); **Actions** gains **Add to lists…**; the remove refusal (3a) links the lists. | `RP-Service`. |
| Services list | The **Lists** column fills; filters gain **List** and the chip "Not in any list · N". | `RP-Services`. |
| Nav, search | Nav: **Lists** `/routing/lists`, order 10. Search: lists by name; meta "routing list · 24 services". | |

## Go signatures

### `routing/own`

```go
type Member struct {
	ServiceID int64
	Tag       string
	Set       snapshot.Set
}
type Server struct {
	Name      string
	Hostnames []string
}
type Drop struct {
	Name   string
	Exact  bool
	Reason string // covered, owned, guarded, pinned
	By     string // the covering or owning tag; the server's name for guarded
	Via    string // the covering suffix; the hostname for guarded; the comment for pinned
}
type Owned struct {
	ServiceID     int64
	Tag           string
	Suffix, Exact []string // what targets install under the tag, sorted
	Total         int      // names in its snapshot
	Dropped       []Drop
}
func (o Owned) Count() int
type Result struct {
	Services []Owned // in list order, one per member
}
func (r Result) Count() int // owned names, all services
// Compute applies the guard, the exclusions (name → reason text) and ADR 0013.
func Compute(members []Member, servers []Server, exclude map[string]string) Result
// Covering reports the server whose hostname the name equals or covers.
func Covering(name string, exact bool, servers []Server) (server, hostname string, ok bool)
type Cover struct {
	Tag   string // the other service
	Via   string // its name that covers (the same name or a suffix above)
	Exact bool
}
// CoveredBy lists the other members that hold the name or a suffix above it.
func CoveredBy(name string, exact bool, members []Member, except int64) []Cover
// Moved lists the names whose owner differs between two results of one list
// (a reorder's "14 domains change owner").
type Move struct {
	Name     string
	Exact    bool
	From, To string // tags; "" when not installed
}
func Moved(before, after Result) []Move
```

### `routing/lists`

```go
var (
	ErrNotFound   = errors.New("lists: no such list")
	ErrDefault    = errors.New("lists: the default list can't be deleted")
	ErrStaleOrder = errors.New("lists: the services changed meanwhile")
	ErrNotMember  = errors.New("lists: the service is not in the list")
)
type GuardError struct{ List, Service, Domain, Server, Hostname string }
type HasTargetsError struct{ Targets []string } // "Home (router)", "iphone (Shadowrocket)"

type List struct {
	ID          int64
	Name        string
	Description string
	Default     bool
	CreatedAt   time.Time
}
type Row struct { // the lists page
	List
	Services int
	Domains  int      // owned names
	Targets  []Target // 3d, 3e
	Warnings int
}
type Target struct {
	Kind  string // router, shadowrocket
	ID    int64
	Name  string
	State string // the target's status word from its row; 3d and 3e word it
}
type Member struct {
	Position int
	Service  services.Item
	Snapshot services.Snapshot // accepted
	Owned    own.Owned
}
type View struct {
	List    List
	Members []Member
	Result  own.Result
}
type Warning struct {
	Kind string // refused, guarded (3c: rejected, failing)
	At   time.Time
	Text string // rendered for the admin's language
	Href string
}

type Deps struct {
	DB        *db.DB
	Events    *events.Catalog
	Services  *services.Service
	Hostnames servers.ServerHostnames // may be nil
	Marker    change.Marker
	Now       func() time.Time
	Log       *slog.Logger
}
type Service struct{ /* … */ }
func New(d Deps) *Service

func (s *Service) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Row, error)
func (s *Service) Get(ctx context.Context, id int64) (List, error)
func (s *Service) Default(ctx context.Context) (List, error)
func (s *Service) Create(ctx context.Context, name, description, actor string) (int64, error) // store.FieldErrors
func (s *Service) Edit(ctx context.Context, id int64, name, description, actor string) (changed bool, err error)
func (s *Service) MakeDefault(ctx context.Context, id int64, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Delete(ctx context.Context, id, moveTo int64, actor string) error // ErrDefault, *HasTargetsError
func (s *Service) Targets(ctx context.Context, id int64) ([]Target, error)
func (s *Service) View(ctx context.Context, id int64, exclude map[string]string) (View, error)
func (s *Service) Add(ctx context.Context, id int64, serviceIDs []int64, actor string) error // *GuardError
func (s *Service) AddTx(ctx context.Context, tx *sqlx.Tx, id int64, serviceIDs []int64, actor string) error // for Add service and the import (3d)
func (s *Service) Remove(ctx context.Context, id, serviceID int64, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Move(ctx context.Context, id, serviceID int64, down bool, actor string) (before, after own.Result, err error)
func (s *Service) SetOrder(ctx context.Context, id int64, serviceIDs, expect []int64, actor string) (own.Result, own.Result, error) // ErrStaleOrder; expect nil: any current order; returns before and after for the band
func (s *Service) ListsOf(ctx context.Context, serviceID int64) ([]List, error)
func (s *Service) Warnings(ctx context.Context, id int64) ([]Warning, error)
// CheckService is services.Deps.Check: the guard over every list holding the service.
func (s *Service) CheckService(ctx context.Context, tx *sqlx.Tx, serviceID int64, set snapshot.Set) error
// CheckSet is the guard for a set about to join these lists (a new service).
func (s *Service) CheckSet(ctx context.Context, tag string, set snapshot.Set, listIDs []int64) error
// AddNew prepares a new upstream service, checks the guard and, in one Write,
// creates it and adds it to the lists.
func (s *Service) AddNew(ctx context.Context, sel string, listIDs []int64, actor string) (int64, error)
// RecordRefusal records list_refused_server_hostname for each list of err, in its own Write.
func (s *Service) RecordRefusal(ctx context.Context, err *GuardError, lists []int64, actor string) error
// Covering is servers.RoutingGuard.Covering over every listed name.
func (s *Service) Covering(ctx context.Context, hostnames []string) ([]servers.RoutedName, error)
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /routing/lists` | Lists |
| `GET /routing/lists/new`, `POST /routing/lists` | New list → its page |
| `GET /routing/lists/:id` | List page |
| `GET /routing/lists/:id/edit`, `POST /routing/lists/:id/edit` | Name, description |
| `POST /routing/lists/:id/default` | Make default |
| `GET /routing/lists/:id/add`, `POST /routing/lists/:id/services` | Add services (`service=<id>` repeated) |
| `POST /routing/lists/:id/services/:service/remove` | Remove (strength 1) |
| `POST /routing/lists/:id/services/:service/move` | `dir=up\|down` |
| `POST /routing/lists/:id/services/order` | `order=<id>,<id>,…` (`expect=` for Undo) |
| `GET /routing/lists/:id/delete`, `POST /routing/lists/:id/delete` | Delete (`move_to` when targets follow it) → `/routing/lists` |
| `GET /routing/services/:id/lists`, `POST /routing/services/:id/lists` | Add a service to lists (`list=<id>` repeated) |

## Pages

- **Routing lists** (`RP-Lists`): title block with "A list is an ordered set of services. Each router and each Shadowrocket config follows one list and sends its domains through the tunnel.", **New list** (primary, `n`) and (3d) **Import from mtvpn…**. Rows (`data-row`, `data-href`): list (name; under it "default for new targets" or the description), services, domains, targets (each with its status marker and state; "none" until 3d/3e), warnings ("▲ 1 left out" in gold, or "none").
- **New list**: a page styled as a dialog: name, description.
- **Routing list** (`RP-List`): crumbs **Lists / Main**; the name; the status line "24 services · 3 412 domains · default for new targets"; **Add services…** (primary, `n`). Areas, in this DOM order (desktop: Services left, the rest right; phone: one column):
  1. **Services, in order** with the note "a domain belongs to the first service that has it" and "Drag, or J K on the selected row, to reorder. Targets get the new order on their next sync." A `[data-sortable]` list: handle ⋮⋮, position, tag (link to the service; the selector under it for upstream), owned / total (the total muted when equal), source, state ("ok" until 3c), ↑ ↓ (`data-key="K"`/`"J"`, `data-row-only`), **Remove** (×, strength 1: "Take anthropic out of Main? Its names leave the targets of Main on their next sync, unless another service in Main has them."). Empty: "No services yet. Targets following Main get nothing from Proxier." with **Add services…**.
  2. **Targets · N**: routers and Shadowrocket configs following it (3d, 3e), else "No routers or Shadowrocket configs follow Main yet."
  3. **Warnings · N**: each warning with its time and a link (the service or the refusal's list).
  4. **Actions**: Rename…, Make default (hidden on the default), Delete… (each with its one-line consequence).
  5. **Activity**: the last 10 events of `routing_list:<id>`.
- **Delete list**: a page styled as a dialog. The default: the reason and no button. With targets: their names and a select "Move them to" (the other lists) with **Move and delete Parents**. Otherwise strength 2: "Delete Parents? Its 6 services stay; only the list goes."

## Events

Recorded in 3b: `routing.list_created`, `routing.list_updated`, `routing.list_deleted`, `routing.list_refused_server_hostname`; `routing.router_updated` and `routing.shadowrocket_updated` when a delete moves targets.

## Doc changes in the same commit

- `docs/processes/routing/routing-lists.md`: ownership's first step (guarded and pinned names are taken out first and cover nothing); names under a service's own suffixes stay; the guard refuses adding a service and saving a custom service, and leaves a name out (with a warning) when a refresh brings it; **Add** appends in tag order; reorder by drag, `J`/`K` or ↑/↓; a list's delete can move its targets in the same step.
- `docs/modules/routing.md#routing-lists`: the same rules in short; owned / total.
- `docs/modules/servers.md` (ports) and `docs/architecture.md` (ports table): `ServerHostnames` lists servers with their hostnames (services hold no IPs, so routing doesn't use them); the new `RoutingGuard` port from routing to servers.
- `docs/processes/servers/server-provisioning.md`: the form refuses a hostname a routing list covers.
- `docs/events.md#routing`: the list events' payloads.

## As built

Built 2026-10-09 in one context. Every checklist line has its test of that name in that file; `make check`, `make lint` and `docker build .` are green. Every package of the module still runs under `-race` (the integration tests use `serverstest` with `StubProxy`, no XHTTP traffic).

**Packages** as in Files, except `routingtest.WithServers` lives in `routingtest/withservers.go`, the list texts in `routing/messages_lists.go` (merged into the module's catalog by `init`), and `pages/newserver_test.go` is new in servers. `cmd/proxier/main.go` calls `srv.SetRouting(rt.Guard())`. CSS for the new rows (`.row.rlist`, `.row.pick`, `.row.warn`, `.band.undo`, `.dropped`, `.cover-hint`) is in the platform's `app.css`; the list page's members reuse 2a's `.row.member`.

**Deviations and additions** (the contract's signatures otherwise hold):

- `own`: the reasons are constants `own.ReasonCovered/ReasonOwned/ReasonGuarded/ReasonPinned` (`Owned` is also the type's name). **Ownership goes to the first service that installs a name**, not the first that lists it: when the earlier service's copy is itself covered by a later service's broader suffix (`mail` with `mail.google.com` before `google` with `google.com` and `mail.google.com`), the later service keeps its own copy instead of dropping it as "owned by mail". `own.Result.Guarded()` lists the guarded names (the list's warnings). `CoveredBy` also reports another member's equal exact name for an exact row; a name with no dot above it (a TLD) is never a parent (`domain.Parents`).
- `lists.GuardError` carries `ListIDs` (the lists the change would have broken), so `Refused` can record one refusal per list. `services.Deps` gains `Refused func(ctx, err, actor)`, called by `SaveCustom` after a transaction `Check` refused; the module wires it to `lists.Refused`, which records through `RecordRefusal` on a context without cancellation. `lists.Add` and `AddNew` record their own refusals.
- `lists` additions: `ErrMoveTo` (Delete's `moveTo` is the list itself or gone), `All` (every list, the default first, then by name), `Size`, `Memberships(serviceID)` (`{List, Position}`; `ListsOf` is built on it), `Refused`. `Target.State` is the row's own word (`active`/`paused`/… for routers, `enabled`/`disabled` for configs) until 3d/3e word it.
- `list_updated` payloads also carry `changes`: `services` (added/removed), `order` (reordered), `default`, or the fields (`name, description`, with `from`/`to` on a rename). The page's Activity words them with `lists.event.{added,removed,reordered,default,fields}`. Edits mark nothing (a name changes nothing targets get); adds, removes and reorders mark `Change{Lists}`; a delete that moves routers marks `Change{Routers}`.
- `services.Prepared.Stored()` is the selector's stored spelling; `Prepare` re-parses the pinned spelling so `Selector` is what is stored. `services.Filter.List`/`NoList` now filter; the services list has chips "in Main", … and "Not in any list · N" (`?list=<id>|none`, pressing a pressed chip clears it).
- servers: `RoutedName` and `RoutingGuard` are aliases of `provision.RoutedName`/`provision.RoutingGuard` (provision can't import the root package). `provision.Deps.Routing` is read at use; the guard is asked in `check` with the computed hostname, so the **live summary** shows the refusal while the admin types as well as `Create` (field `routing`, key `servers.err.routed` with `host, domain, service, list`; a guard error is `servers.err.routing_check`).
- `Covering` (provisioning) walks every list (the default first) and every member in order and gives **one hit per hostname**; any listed name counts, installed or not.
- Pages: the list page's DOM order is Services, Targets, Warnings, Actions, Activity. **Add service** (`/routing/services/add`) gains the list checkboxes (the default ticked); with lists ticked it calls `AddNew`; `from_list=1` (the list picker's "Or add a new one") redirects back to the list with `?added=1`. The "taken" area's "add a separate one" form carries the ticked lists. The picker filter is an htmx GET with `hx-select="#pick-rows"`. The Undo band names "Moved X above Y / below Y" from the one service that moved (the first that went up, else the first that went down). The editor's hint is the first covering member per row; the footer names every list holding the service. The remove page links each list.

**Facts later sub-phases rely on.**

- `lists.View(ctx, id, exclude)` is the one view of what targets get: members in order (`services.Item`, the accepted `services.Snapshot`, `own.Owned`) and `Result`. 3d renders from `Result.Services[i].Suffix/Exact` under `Tag`; 3e passes the router's infra pins as `exclude` (name → reason text, shown as "left out: <reason>").
- `lists.AddTx` is the import's (3d) and discovery's (3g) way into a list inside their own transaction: it checks the guard (returns `*GuardError`, the caller records with `Refused` after its rollback), appends in tag order, records `list_updated{added}` and marks.
- `lists.Delete` moves routers and configs through `store.MoveRouter/MoveShadowrocket` and records `router_updated{changes: list, from, to}` / `shadowrocket_updated{changes: list, from, to}`; 3e's router page should word the same payload.
- `store.ListTargets` reads routers then configs by name; 3d/3e's Targets areas and the lists page column read it through `lists.Targets`.
- The guard's servers come from `ServerHostnames.Servers` once per call; nothing is cached.

**Not done / the user's.** A real-browser look at the new pages (drag, `J`/`K`, ↑/↓, the Undo band and `u`, the picker's filter, the phone width): headless Chrome would not start in this session either (no output within 20 s), so they were exercised only through the HTTP tests. No real server was provisioned against a routing list.
